answer: Stake-weighted voting with quadratic payouts resists Sybils: each agent locks a bond in the lotus pool, and influence grows only with the square root of stake, so ten clones get barely more than one honest agent while paying ten separate bonds. Detected collusion slashes every linked bond, starting a spiral of lost trust that makes each new fake identity worth less than the last. Facing a rising tide of forfeited collateral and shrinking returns, the attacker's cost outruns any possible gain.
